import sys, json, hashlib, datetime

# The fast lane. Four recipes, rendered from parameters that `classify` has
# already validated. No model, no network, no disk: what leaves here is a string
# built out of a dict.

# --8<-- digest-helper
def canonical(declarations):
    # Canonical bytes: keys sorted, no spaces, no ascii escaping. The digest has
    # to survive a round trip through a CHAT -- the draft is shown to a human,
    # the model repeats it in the second tool call, and the submitter refuses
    # anything whose bytes changed on the way. Without that, the manifest a
    # human said yes to and the manifest that gets applied are only PROBABLY
    # the same one.
    return json.dumps(declarations, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                      ensure_ascii=False)


def digest(declarations):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(declarations).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
# --8<-- end

# GH #480 -- the same six coordinates `templates/builder/weave` writes down when
# a composer opens a round. They are named here because the FAST LANE opens no
# round: there is no model call behind a recipe, so nothing on this lane ever
# reached the round table, and a refusal that came back for a model-free build
# found no owner for its digest and no door to answer to.
CALLER_KEYS = ("build_call_id", "agent", "build_op", "build_scope",
               "build_caller", "build_auto_submit")


def rewire_edge(p):
    edge = {"from": p["from"], "to": p["to"]}
    if p.get("condition"):
        edge["condition"] = p["condition"]
    # Remove FIRST. A manifest rolls forward and stops at the first refusal,
    # with no rollback (R5): an add that lands before its remove leaves both
    # edges live if the remove is then refused, which is a silent fan-out, not
    # a rewire.
    return [
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {},
         "diff": {"remove_edges": [{"match": {"from": p["from"], "to": p["old_to"]}}]}},
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {}, "diff": {"add_edges": [edge]}},
    ]


def add_node(p):
    # `add_timer` was the third recipe in the plan; the tree ships no standalone
    # timer template, and inventing one to make a recipe true would be the tail
    # wagging the dog. The class it stood for -- grow a cell and wire it in --
    # survives with the template as a PARAMETER, which makes the recipe useful
    # for every single-cell template instead of exactly one.
    node = {"name": p["name"], "template": p["template"]}
    if isinstance(p.get("override_params"), dict):
        node["override_params"] = p["override_params"]
    return [
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {}, "diff": {"add_nodes": [node]}},
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {},
         "diff": {"add_edges": [{"from": "./" + p["name"], "to": p["target"],
                                 "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'%s'" % p["route"]}}}]}},
    ]


def attach_drain(p):
    return [{"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {},
             "diff": {"add_edges": [{"from": p["from"], "to": p["to"],
                 "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == '%s'" % p["route"]}]}}]



# --- the round a channel speaks in (GH #517) --------------------------------
#
# A round is PROVENANCE, and provenance is not derived. Until this repair the
# channel level read the member's identity off the DIRECTORY NAME of the scope
# the wish had named -- `.../members/egon` became `member:egon` -- which is the
# right answer only while the folder happens to be spelled like the person.
# Where it was not, the ingress edge declared a round that exists in no row of
# the store, and the audience gate (`memory-hive/recall`, `visible()`,
# `audience_now` subset of `row_audience`) refused every single one of them:
# 34 facts, 182 episodes, four legs, ZERO candidates, and a bundle saying
# "Nothing in this memory answers this question" -- the same sentence a
# genuinely empty store produces. Silent, total, and indistinguishable from
# having no memory at all (measured on a live colony, GH #517).
#
# So the person is a thing the WISH says. It travels in the declaration's own
# `ctx` block under `member_person`, and a wish that does not say it is ASKED
# rather than guessed at. `ctx` is where it lives for a second reason: the
# claim then stands in the rendered manifest, in front of the reviewer, before
# it is committed -- and the mutation door ignores a ctx key no template of the
# declaration requires (`validate::check_declared_requirements` reads the
# template's REQUIRED keys and nothing else).
#
# `templates/receptionist/greet` already writes the rule this recipe broke: a
# door that was told no audience leaves it EMPTY -- "a channel identity is a
# room, not a participant, and turning one into the other would invent a member
# nobody named". A recipe cannot leave it empty, because an empty round is
# refused by the holders; so it asks.
#
# THE OTHER HALF IS NOT THE SAME DEFECT. `agent:<assistant>` is built from
# `p["assistant"]`, which is a PARAMETER OF THE WISH -- "the agent this
# channel's turns default to" -- and not a string carved out of a path. It is
# the one name the wish is already required to say (LEVEL_EXTRA["channel"]), so
# it is a quotation, not a guess. A generation whose affinity identity differs
# from the node it stands in is a case nobody has yet had; when it appears it
# is a second ctx key here, not a derivation.
PERSON_KEY = "member_person"

# The question, verbatim on the wire. A refusal a human cannot read is one they
# cannot answer -- the same rule `normalise` follows when a composer asks for a
# model id instead of inventing one.
PERSON_QUESTION = (
    "who is the PERSON this channel speaks with? A channel's ingress edge "
    "declares the round every turn on it is spoken in -- "
    "[\"agent:<assistant>\", \"member:<person>\"] in affinity vocabulary -- "
    "and that round decides which rows of the member's memory the turn is "
    "allowed to see. It is the person's identity, which is NOT necessarily the "
    "name of the directory the member stands in. Name it as "
    "ctx.%s of the wish." % PERSON_KEY)


class WishIncomplete(Exception):
    """A fact the recipe was not given and will not invent.

    It is not a KeyError, because `recipe_params_incomplete` means "you named a
    recipe and left a parameter out" and this one means "the wish never said".
    They call for opposite repairs: one is a typo in a tool call, the other is a
    question for whoever made the wish.
    """

    def __init__(self, key, question):
        Exception.__init__(self, question)
        self.key = key
        self.question = question


# --- birth ------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# `add_nodes[].birth` (GH #437) decides whether what a declaration places comes
# to the world registered, addressable and TASKLESS or registered and running.
# It is the DOOR's vocabulary and not this recipe's -- `active` (the door's own
# default) or `inactive`, and a third word is refused here rather than carried,
# because the door refuses it too and a manifest that stops halfway through is
# the expensive way to learn about a typo.
BIRTH_STATES = ("active", "inactive")

# The one level whose default is not the door's. A connector opens its upstream
# the moment it has a task -- so a channel grown from a wish is born ASLEEP and
# armed by a second, deliberate act (GH #468), and the wish that wants it awake
# says so and gets `active` written out rather than left to a default. Every
# other level is a composition of cells that wait to be addressed, and waking
# one costs nothing.
LEVEL_BIRTH = {"channel": "inactive"}


# --- grow_level -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A LEVEL is a recipe, because the edges a new child gets are a property of the
# PARENT and not of the child. `examples/organism` writes them out by hand, once
# per child, and the COUNTS are published exactly once, in the README table of
# this template, with a test deriving them from this renderer. They are not a
# coincidence and not a judgement -- they are the same set every time, with the
# child's name substituted in.
#
# WHY A TABLE AND NOT A DERIVATION. The obvious idea is to compute the set from
# the child's `contract.accepts` / `contract.emits`. It does not work, and the
# reason is worth writing down so nobody re-derives the disappointment:
#
#   * A connector has NO contract at all. `telegram-connector` is a `proxy`
#     cell, its `accepts` and `emits` are both empty, and its two upward edges
#     condition on `has(hop.error_code)` -- on a failure key, not on a lane.
#   * Lane count is not edge count, in both directions. `assistant@2.5.0`
#     declares twenty-two rim lanes and four more on corridors, and gets
#     twenty-three edges: `in_advice`, `in_sweep`, `in_prune` and
#     `in_round_sweep` are addressed at the path
#     directly (ruling W7-R5), `in_pack` and `pack_ack` are the opt-in
#     identity door and not part of the level (GH #473), and `display` folds
#     `event`+`receipt` into ONE edge one level further out.
#   * Guards, modifiers and literals live in no contract. `context.assistant ==
#     '<name>'`, the `audience_set` literal, `hop.owner.contains(...)`, the
#     `set_hop.route = 'in_view'` restamp -- addressing is a property of the
#     parent, and `params.contract` has no vocabulary for it.
#
# So: a table, pinned against `examples/organism/grow-*.json` byte for byte by
# `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh466_grow_level_renders_the_level.rs`. The example
# and the recipe cannot drift apart, because one is generated from the other's
# table and compared.
#
# WHAT STAYS WITH THE MODEL. The TEMPLATE. This recipe renders edges; it does
# not choose what to grow. Which template a level is filled with is a catalogue
# question, and the catalogue is the librarian's -- the design lane looks it up,
# the fast lane is TOLD it. Same for `ctx`: the recipe passes whatever it was
# given straight into the declaration and asserts nothing about it, because the
# authority on what a template demands is the mutation door, which answers
# `requirement_missing` by name and hands it back on `in_receipt`.


# --- the narrow form, and the scope root a level asks for (GH #503) ----------
#
# A level DECLARES ITSELF AT THE CONTAINER it grows into -- `/os/orgs` for an
# organisation, `<member>/assistants` for an assistant -- and names its child
# bare. Until #503 the declaration stood one storey higher: the scope was the
# container's PARENT and the container travelled inside the node name
# (`orgs/acme`, `./orgs -> ./orgs/acme`). Both forms grow the same tree; the
# absolute edges are identical to the byte. What moves is the declaration's
# SCOPE ROOT, and the scope root is what the broker judges.
#
# That is the whole defect. `templates/access/store/seed/policy.jsonl` grants
# `colony.mutate.default` under `scope_prefix: "/os/orgs"`, and the FIRST
# organisation of a colony is grown at `/os` -- so the one build every colony
# starts with was refused at the front with `requester_not_permitted`, while
# the very same manifest applied by an operator committed. Every other level
# was already under the prefix and never noticed.
#
# Drawable at all only since GH #487: `.` (and `./`) resolves to the
# declaration's own scope inside `add_edges`, so a container can be addressed
# from the declaration that stands in it. Before that, the wide spelling was
# the only one the door accepted.
#
# ONE FORM FOR EVERY LEVEL, with one measured exception -- the identity door of
# `_assistant_level`, which reaches a hive that is the container's SIBLING and
# is therefore not addressable from inside it at all. See there.


class Place(object):
    """Where a level's declaration stands, and how it spells its child.

    `container` is the hive the child is placed in, and it is the real name in
    both forms: a guard that reads an absolute path (`hop.owner`) names the
    TREE, not the declaration it was written in. `narrow` is whether the
    declaration stands at that hive (the form above) or one storey above it.
    """

    def __init__(self, container, narrow):
        self.container = container
        self.narrow = narrow

    def up(self):
        """The container -- `.` when the declaration already stands in it."""
        return "." if self.narrow else "./" + self.container

    def down(self, name):
        """The child, as an edge endpoint."""
        return ("./" + name) if self.narrow else "./%s/%s" % (self.container, name)

    def node(self, name):
        """The child, as `add_nodes[].name`."""
        return name if self.narrow else "%s/%s" % (self.container, name)

    def scope(self, parent):
        """The declaration's scope, from the scope the WISH named.

        The recipe PARAMETER stays what it always was -- the parent the wish
        talks about ("grow an org under /os"). Only the rendered declaration
        moves down into the container, because that is the address the edges
        are relative to.
        """
        if not self.narrow:
            return parent
        base = str(parent).rstrip("/")
        return "%s/%s" % (base, self.container) if base else "/" + self.container


def _in(place, name, route, guard=""):
    return {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == '%s'%s" % (route, guard)}


def _out(place, name, route):
    return {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == '%s'" % route}


# The key a container level is ADDRESSED by, one per level. `Edge.to` is a static
# path in this substrate, so two children of one container cost two edges and
# each one has to say WHICH child it is for -- the address rule of this
# template's README, read one storey above the assistant it was written for.
# Until GH #478 the six doors below carried the lane and nothing else, which is
# an address only while a container holds exactly one child; with two, every
# message on the lane is delivered TWICE.
CONTAINER_KEY = {"orgs": "org", "members": "member"}


def _container_level(place, name, _p):
    # org and member are the SAME shape one level apart, and that is a claim
    # about their two contracts rather than a convenience: org@1.4.0 and
    # member@1.6.0 declare the same eight RIM accepts and the same thirteen
    # RIM emits -- member's three v-lane pairs touch no container edge --
    # and each one's parent already carries every one of those lanes into
    # the container its child is grown into. Seven doors down, thirteen
    # exits back up.
    #
    # `in_import` is the ONE accept that gets NO edge, which is the rule
    # above read once more: an import addresses the level's OWN path, so an
    # edge from the container could never deliver one -- and a member already
    # running is the only thing it is for (`examples/memory-import/`, edges()).
    #
    # The ORDER is the one `build_import.py` writes. That tool is the second
    # generator of this very set, and the two are compared element for element
    # by `gh470_a_grown_container_level_carries_its_export_lanes.rs` -- so the
    # order is not a style choice here either, it is what makes the comparison
    # a comparison. This table stood at thirteen edges from before the member
    # had a memory export (GH #470); nothing was red, because the byte pin
    # compared it against examples generated from itself.
    #
    # The discriminator is PERMISSIVE and not strict (GH #478). Nothing in a
    # grown topology promotes `context.member` or `context.org` today, so
    # `has(...) && ... == name` would strand every existing colony's turns at
    # the container the day it landed. Without the key the fan-out is what it
    # always was; with it, the turn reaches exactly one child. It is the form
    # `_assistant_level` already writes for `in_build_result`, and the one
    # `templates/meclaw-os/config.json` uses for `context.build_caller`.
    key = CONTAINER_KEY[place.container]
    guard = " && (!has(context.%s) || context.%s == '%s')" % (key, key, name)
    edges = [_in(place, name, r, guard)
             for r in ("in_turn", "in_recall", "in_brief", "in_propose",
                       "in_build_result", "in_export")]
    # GH #553 -- the mutation receipt. It carries the SAME permissive guard the
    # six doors above carry, and that is not a formality: two children of one
    # container may never share a door under one condition (GH #478), or the
    # edge table cannot tell them apart. What makes the receipt a FAN-OUT
    # anyway is that it carries no context at all -- the permissive half of the
    # guard is true for every child, so every one of them hears that the graph
    # moved, which is exactly right: each has a tool menu or a picture that
    # follows from it.
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "mutation_committed", guard))
    edges += [_out(place, name, r)
              for r in ("answer", "bundle", "ack", "reject", "error", "write",
                        "turn_write", "prune", "build", "close_report",
                        "export_done", "dump", "pack_ack")]
    return edges


def _assistant_level(place, name, p):
    # The address rule, v1 (GH #454): ONE edge per assistant, guarded on
    # `context.assistant`, because `Edge.to` is a static path in this substrate.
    # There is no edge meaning "send it wherever the context says", and there
    # will not be one -- so N assistants cost N edges and never N x M.
    guard = " && has(context.assistant) && context.assistant == '%s'" % name
    edges = [_in(place, name, "in_turn", guard)]
    # GH #553 -- the mutation receipt, on the PERMISSIVE form of the guard, the
    # one `in_build_result` below already uses: two generations of one member
    # may not share a door under one condition (GH #478), and a receipt carries
    # no `context.assistant`, so the permissive half is true for both and every
    # generation hears that the graph moved. The assistant carries it on into
    # `./talky` and `./cogny` itself, and each of those into its own collector.
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "mutation_committed",
                     " && (!has(context.assistant) || context.assistant == '%s')" % name))
    # GH #562 -- the memory road is a V-LANE (ADR-0020) and is the one part of
    # this set that does not end on the generation's path. `recall` leaves the
    # ASKER (`<gen>/talky`, `<gen>/cogny`) and `in_bundle` goes straight back
    # down to the one the reply-to token names; the generation's contract names
    # both askers under `at`, which is the permission, and the four edges the
    # chain used to need here are two. The stamps ride ON the v-lane: they used
    # to sit on the generation's own rim, and the rim is not in the road any
    # more. The two doors back keep the shape GH #532 gave them -- the core's
    # guarded on `hop.recall_caller`, the surface's the `default`, so a bundle
    # with no token or an unknown one lands where every bundle landed before.
    for asker in ("cogny", "talky"):
        door = {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name) + "/" + asker,
                "lane": "in_bundle",
                "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'in_bundle'"
                             + guard}
        if asker == "cogny":
            door["condition"] += (" && has(hop.recall_caller) && "
                                  "hop.recall_caller == 'cogny'")
        else:
            door["default"] = True
        edges.append(door)
    edges += [_out(place, name, "answer")]
    for asker, drops in (("talky", ["col_phase", "consult_class",
                                    "consult_id", "tool_answerer"]),
                         ("cogny", ["col_phase", "consult_class",
                                    "tool_answerer"])):
        edges.append({"from": place.down(name) + "/" + asker,
                      "to": place.up(),
                      "lane": "recall",
                      "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'recall'",
                      "modifier": {
                          "set_context": {"recall_caller": "'%s'" % asker},
                          "delete_context": drops}})
    # GH #552 -- the memory TOOL road, and it is deliberately NOT a v-lane.
    # `memory_recall` leaves the generation as an ordinary `tool` the level's
    # own named edge took out of the default, so the ADDRESS on the way back is
    # the generation and not one of its two brains: `context.tool_caller` was
    # stamped on the way out and the generation's own two entry edges read it.
    # The member is the mandatory hop either way -- it is the level that knows
    # the round the question is asked in -- and a template edge is one an audit
    # can read off disk, which four v-lanes of the recall road are not.
    #
    # The two exits STAMP the generation, exactly as `build` does, and the two
    # doors read it permissively, exactly as `in_build_result` does: a menu tick
    # starts at a timer inside the generation and carries no `context.assistant`
    # of its own, so without the stamp the memory's declaration would come back
    # to every generation in this container.
    for lane in ("tool", "schemas"):
        exit_edge = _out(place, name, lane)
        exit_edge["modifier"] = {"set_context": {"assistant": "'%s'" % name}}
        edges.append(exit_edge)
    for lane in ("in_tool", "in_menu"):
        edges.append(_in(place, name, lane,
                         " && (!has(context.assistant) || context.assistant == '%s')" % name))
    edges += [_out(place, name, r)
              for r in ("extraction", "write",
                        "turn_write", "prune", "error")]
    build = _out(place, name, "build")
    build["modifier"] = {"set_context": {"assistant": "'%s'" % name}}
    edges.append(build)
    # A build result with NO assistant on the context belongs to whoever asked;
    # one that names an assistant belongs to that one alone.
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "in_build_result",
                     " && (!has(context.assistant) || context.assistant == '%s')" % name))
    # GH #476 -- the transfer lanes GH #475 opened. A generation holds ONE store
    # its member cannot recompute: the session ledger four levels down in its
    # own `session-keeper`, which decides whether a conversation continues or
    # starts at zero. `in_export` and `in_import` are addressed with the SAME
    # key a turn is, because a member with two generations has two ledgers and
    # they are not one document -- and a document is filed under the hive it
    # came out of, so two keepers would write one directory.
    #
    # TWO ways back, and both are PLAIN. Since GH #555 the keeper's own store
    # writes the seed set and the keeper says `export_done` itself; what still
    # travels on `dump` is the receipt of an applied import part. Every level
    # between this container and the keeper pairs `in_export` with `export_done`
    # and `in_import` with `dump` in `params.required_drains`, and the probe
    # that checks a pairing runs the described hop through the real edge
    # evaluator -- an edge that additionally tested a second hop key evaluates
    # false under it and reads as no drain at all, so the mutation is refused.
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "in_export", guard))
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "in_import", guard))
    edges.append(_out(place, name, "export_done"))
    edges.append(_out(place, name, "dump"))
    # GH #473 -- the identity door, and it is OPT-IN rather than part of the
    # level. A grown assistant reaches its brain with an EMPTY `system` tree:
    # nothing in a grown topology writes a durable slot, and the one lane that
    # can (`in_pack`, GH #458) has to be drawn from the member's own record.
    #
    # Two edges, the shape `templates/affinity/README.md` publishes: the push
    # leaves the affinity HIVE on `answer` and is told apart from the tool lane
    # by `hop.subscriber`, restamped onto the subscriber's own `in_pack`; and
    # `in_pack` and `pack_ack` are ONE decision, so the drain is drawn in the
    # same breath or the door refuses both with `required_drain_missing`.
    #
    # WHY OPT-IN. The act has an owner. Since GH #479 the submitter's form
    # check has a second branch for exactly this shape -- a parent may draw an
    # `in_pack` edge into a node the SAME declaration creates -- so a level that
    # always drew one would in fact be submittable. It stays a parameter because
    # writing into a brain's prompt is not something a level does to every
    # generation grown from it without being asked. (Before #479 the rule had one
    # branch, `subscribe_target_not_self` fired on every grown door, and the
    # opt-in had no reachable caller at all.) The ROW is
    # the other half and is not renderable at all: a `subscribers` row is a
    # store write, and writing it stays a `subscribe` op through affinity's own
    # gate (ruling R-Subscribe). What this renders is the half a manifest can
    # carry -- the graph the row will need.
    #
    # WHY THIS ONE LEVEL KEEPS THE WIDE FORM (GH #503, and it is measured).
    # `./affinity` is a SIBLING of `./assistants`, one storey up. From a
    # declaration standing IN the container the only spellings that could reach
    # it are `../affinity` and an absolute path, and `mutation::validate` refuses
    # both in an edge endpoint outright (`ScopeOutOfBounds`, and the `..` arm is
    # a security hotfix rather than a lookup miss) -- so in the narrow form the
    # affinity hive is not addressable at all. Splitting the door into a SECOND
    # declaration at the member does not survive either: `templates/submit/gate`
    # accepts an `in_pack` edge only when its target is under the requester or
    # is created by THAT SAME declaration, the requester of a grown door is
    # `/os/operator/intake` (GH #479, re-read after GH #556: the submitter moved
    # INTO the front door, so the cell whose emission a grown door is attributed
    # to is the intake occupant beside it), and a declaration that only draws
    # edges creates nothing -- measured, it comes back
    # `subscribe_target_not_self`.
    # Widening that check is a change to a security default and wants its own
    # ruling, which is exactly what #503 says option 3 is.
    #
    # The trade is free where it lands: an assistant is grown at
    # `/os/orgs/<org>/members/<member>`, which is under the broker's
    # `/os/orgs` prefix in EITHER form. Nothing reachable becomes unreachable.
    #
    # WHAT THE DOOR IS, SINCE GH #561. Four edges, and every one of them a
    # V-LANE (GH #559): two in, one per BRAIN RIM of the generation, and two
    # back for the receipts. It used to be two, both stopping at the generation's
    # own path, with `assistant` fanning the pack out to `./talky` and `./cogny`
    # inside and carrying the two receipts back. That fan-out is gone from the
    # level, because a level that declares a lane and only forwards it claims an
    # influence it never took -- and what is left there is the CONNECT POINT,
    # `"at": ["./talky", "./cogny"]` on both lanes, which is what makes an edge
    # ending two storeys down legal at all. Skip the corridor and the mutation is
    # refused `v_lane_no_connect_point`; end it somewhere the `at` does not name
    # and it is refused the same way. The `lane` field is what turns each of
    # these from an ordinary deep edge into a declared one: it is NAMED rather
    # than guessed, because no validation can read a lane out of a CEL guard.
    #
    # The GUARD still names the SUBSCRIBER and the subscriber is still the
    # GENERATION, not a rim. A subscription is one row about one agent; the
    # fan-out is the two edges, exactly as it was two edges inside the level.
    # `./brief` sets `subscriber` on every answer it speaks -- empty string for
    # the tool lane -- so without the comparison both edges would also collect
    # every brief meant for somebody else.
    #
    # The receipts stop at `./assistants` and not at `.`: the member's own
    # `./assistants -> .` edge on `pack_ack` is its BOUNDARY exit, the same one
    # `write`, `prune` and `error` leave by, and it stands whether or not any
    # generation subscribed. `delete_context` strips the one interior marker a
    # receipt can carry out of a rim (`col_phase`, the collector's phase) -- the
    # level used to strip it on the pass-through that is now gone.
    # GH #543 -- the way back from a SCREEN, and it is part of the level rather
    # than a hand-drawn extra beside it. The member splits `event`/`receipt` on
    # `hop.owner` and hands anything under `/assistants/` to the container; this
    # is the SECOND hop, and it belongs here because the owner names the
    # generation and only the level knows that name. The ordinary `in_turn` door
    # cannot take it: that one is guarded on `context.assistant`, which a screen
    # event never carries, so before this edge existed a view event reached the
    # container and stopped there -- measured on a built colony, where the
    # declaration lived only in `examples/organism/grow-screen.json` and no wish
    # ever rendered it.
    #
    # `/assistants/` stays a LITERAL, exactly as it is in `_app_level`: the guard
    # reads `hop.owner`, which is an absolute path, so it names the TREE and not
    # the declaration it was written in. That holds in the wide form too, where
    # the declaration stands at the member.
    #
    # It is the LAST edge of the level's own set, ahead of both opt-ins, so the
    # indices `subscribe` and `credential` render at do not move.
    #
    # AND IT IS DISJOINT FROM THE DOOR, by construction rather than by luck.
    # `apply_edges` fans out to EVERY matching regular edge -- there is no
    # exactly-one semantics in this substrate -- and `context` is persistent
    # along a trace. A display RECEIPT carries both: the answer that put the view
    # up travelled with `context.assistant`, nothing on the way to the screen
    # deletes it, and the display stamps `hop.owner` on the way back. Both edges
    # would match and the generation would be handed the same receipt twice.
    # So the door keeps `has(context.assistant)` and this one demands its
    # absence: the two conditions are exact complements, and the case this edge
    # exists for is precisely the one with no `context.assistant` -- a screen
    # EVENT, raised by the browser on a fresh trace, which is what a built colony
    # was measured losing at the container.
    edges.append({"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
                  "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'in_turn' && "
                               "!has(context.assistant) && "
                               "has(hop.owner) && hop.owner.contains("
                               "'/assistants/%s/')" % name})
    if p.get("subscribe"):
        target = place.down(name)
        for rim in ("talky", "cogny"):
            edges.append({
                "from": "./affinity", "to": "%s/%s" % (target, rim),
                "lane": "in_pack",
                "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'answer' && "
                             "hop.subscriber == '%s'" % target,
                "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_pack'"}}})
        for rim in ("talky", "cogny"):
            edges.append({
                "from": "%s/%s" % (target, rim), "to": "./assistants",
                "lane": "pack_ack",
                "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'pack_ack'",
                "modifier": {"delete_context": ["col_phase"]}})
    return edges


# --- the credential v-lanes (GH #560) ---------------------------------------
#
# A generation that spends a provider key can be grown so that it holds NONE:
# the key lives in the member's own `access`, and each brain ASKS for it over a
# v-lane (ADR-0020). What this renders is the runnable form
# `examples/organism/grow-credentials.json` carries and
# `templates/member/README.md` § *The credential v-lanes* publishes -- two edges
# per brain, both naming the lane they carry, plus the grants the broker answers
# them out of.
#
# IT IS THE SAME DECLARATION AS THE LEVEL, since GH #567. The lane ends on
# `<gen>/talky/brain`, two levels INSIDE the node `grow_level` gives birth to,
# and the connect point that makes it legal is declared by `talky`/`cogny` --
# not by the generation. Until #567 a mutation read the contract of a hive it
# gives birth to from the template ROOT only, so these four edges drawn beside
# the `add_nodes` that creates their target's GRANDPARENT were refused
# `v_lane_no_connect_point` and had to travel one declaration later. Stage 6
# now reads the whole STAGED SUBTREE with `ref` markers resolved, so the
# declaration that grows the generation is where the road is drawn.
#
# THE ORDER ARGUMENT WENT WITH IT. It used to say: a manifest rolls forward and
# stops at the first refusal with no rollback (R5), so a refusal on the second
# declaration leaves a generation whose brains hold `api_key: ""` and name a
# grant nobody wired -- loudly, because the first turn emits
# `credential_request` onto no edge and dead-letters `no_route`. There is no
# roll-forward between two acts any more: node, edges and grants are judged
# together and land together or not at all. What is left is the rule the level
# already had -- a node that landed without its edges is an island, which is
# the failure this recipe exists to prevent.
#
# WHERE IT STANDS. At the MEMBER, the lowest common ancestor of a brain and the
# broker, because an edge lives in the graph of that level. That is one storey
# above the container an assistant otherwise declares itself in (GH #503), so
# `credential` takes the WIDE form of the level -- the same one `subscribe`
# already takes for the identity door. Both switches at once are still ONE
# declaration: one node, one scope, every edge of both roads behind the
# level's own.
#
# WHAT THE WISH SAYS, AND WHAT THE RENDERER BUILDS. `cred_ref` and `subject` are
# quotations: which credential of the vault, and whose it is. `expires_at` is
# asked for rather than invented -- a horizon is a security decision and the
# recipe has no business picking one. The grant HANDLE is built from those two,
# and that is not a guess in the GH #517 sense: the renderer writes the same
# string into the seed row and into the brain's own `credential_grant_id`, so
# the two ends cannot disagree with each other. It is the shape the member's
# README publishes, `grant:<cred tail>@<subject>/<consumer>` -- ONE grant per
# consumer, because the answer edge is addressed by `hop.grant_id` and two
# brains sharing a handle would each be handed the other's sealed box.
CREDENTIAL_ASKERS = ("talky", "cogny")

# The broker is the member's OWN occupant since `member@1.5.0`, at a fixed name.
# It is not a parameter for the same reason the container of a level is not one:
# a member does not stand its access hive in `./broker` in one colony and
# `./access` in another.
CREDENTIAL_BROKER = "./access"

# The example's number, and the only one this renderer has an opinion about. A
# credential round is one provider call per parked turn, so the cap is a
# runaway guard rather than a quota anybody tunes.
CREDENTIAL_RATE_PER_MIN = 60


def _grant_handle(cred_ref, subject, asker):
    """`grant:<cred tail>@<subject>/<consumer>` -- one per consumer."""
    tail = cred_ref.split(":", 1)[1] if ":" in cred_ref else cred_ref
    return "grant:%s@%s/%s" % (tail.replace(":", "-"),
                               subject.replace(":", "-"), asker)


def _credential_edges(name, cred):
    """The four v-lanes, in the order the example carries them."""
    edges = []
    for asker in CREDENTIAL_ASKERS:
        brain = "./assistants/%s/%s/brain" % (name, asker)
        handle = _grant_handle(cred["cred_ref"], cred["subject"], asker)
        # The ASK. `set_context.requester` is what the broker issues the grant
        # to (R-AC-1) -- a body claiming a requester changes nothing -- and it
        # names the generation and the rim, because one requester is one grant.
        edges.append({
            "from": brain, "to": CREDENTIAL_BROKER,
            "lane": "credential_request",
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'credential_request'",
            "modifier": {
                "set_hop": {"route": "'in_invoke'"},
                "set_context": {"requester": "'agent:%s/%s'" % (name, asker)}}})
        # The ANSWER, addressed by the handle. `vault.deliver` is on the guard
        # beside `ack` because the broker speaks `ack` for every operation it
        # performs, and a policy verdict is not a sealed box.
        edges.append({
            "from": CREDENTIAL_BROKER, "to": brain,
            "lane": "in_sealed",
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'ack' && "
                         "has(hop.operation) && hop.operation == 'vault.deliver'"
                         " && has(hop.grant_id) && hop.grant_id == '%s'" % handle,
            "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_sealed'"}}})
    return edges


def _credential_rows(name, cred, now):
    """The grants and their birth events, through the mutation door.

    `seed_rows` and not a store seed: the door that writes them keeps a
    `mutation_log` row, which is what a permission row deserves. The caveat the
    member's README publishes rides along -- `seed_rows` creates the store's
    `cell.db` when the store has never woken, and a `seed/<table>.jsonl` only
    lands on a fresh database, so a member's broker seeded this way carries none
    of the shipped `policy` rows. For a person's broker that is the right
    outcome: every one of them is about `colony.mutate`.
    """
    grants, events = [], []
    for asker in CREDENTIAL_ASKERS:
        handle = _grant_handle(cred["cred_ref"], cred["subject"], asker)
        grants.append({
            "grant_id": handle,
            "requester": "agent:%s/%s" % (name, asker),
            "capability": "credential.read",
            "subject": cred["subject"],
            "scope": {"actions": ["vault.deliver"]},
            "cred_ref": cred["cred_ref"],
            "purpose": "authenticate %s's %s brain against the provider"
                       % (name, asker),
            "issued_at": now,
            "expires_at": cred["expires_at"],
            "rule_id": cred.get("rule_id") or "credential-read",
            "constraints": {"rate_per_min": int(cred.get("rate_per_min")
                                                or CREDENTIAL_RATE_PER_MIN)}})
        events.append({
            "id": "ev-%s-%s" % (name, asker),
            "grant_id": handle,
            "event": "granted",
            "at": now,
            "actor": "operator",
            "reason_code": "",
            "detail": {"why": "seeded with the level: credential_grant_id "
                              "is immutable, so the grant has to exist before "
                              "the brain that names it ever asks"}})
    return [{"target": "./access/store", "table": "grants", "rows": grants},
            {"target": "./access/store", "table": "grant_events",
             "rows": events}]


def _credential_overrides(given, name, cred):
    """Both params on both brains, merged into whatever the wish already set.

    The empty `api_key` is the SWITCH and not tidiness: a brain asks for a
    credential only while it holds none, and the key in its config counts as
    one. Both keys are immutable, so both are set where the generation is grown
    or not at all -- the repair afterwards is a new generation.
    """
    out = dict(given or {})
    for asker in CREDENTIAL_ASKERS:
        slot = "%s/brain" % asker
        own = dict(out.get(slot) or {})
        own["api_key"] = ""
        own["credential_grant_id"] = _grant_handle(cred["cred_ref"],
                                                   cred["subject"], asker)
        out[slot] = own
    return out


def _channel_level(place, name, p):
    # A connector raises a turn and stamps WHO it is for. The default agent is a
    # literal on the edge on purpose: a CEL guard is evaluated by the substrate
    # against `hop` and `context` and cannot read a node's `params`, so "the
    # default of this channel" has nowhere else to live.
    #
    # GH #517 -- the round is READ OFF THE WISH and never off the scope. See
    # PERSON_KEY above for the failure the old derivation produced.
    agent = p["assistant"]
    ctx = p.get("ctx") if isinstance(p.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
    person = str(ctx.get(PERSON_KEY) or "").strip()
    if not person:
        raise WishIncomplete(PERSON_KEY, PERSON_QUESTION)
    # GH #517 -- every promotion on this edge is `has(...) ? ... : ''`, which is
    # the rule `templates/member/README.md` already publishes for the doors one
    # storey up: a modifier that fails to evaluate SKIPS THE WHOLE EDGE, and a
    # turn that vanishes on an edge is invisible, while a turn that arrives with
    # an empty key is refused by the holder on a lane that is drained, with a
    # reason. The bare `hop.chat_id` this edge used to carry logged
    # `cel eval set_context.chat_id: No such key: chat_id` on every emission the
    # connector makes that is not an inbound message -- its own failures ride
    # the second edge below, and they carry no chat.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "!has(hop.error_code)",
         "modifier": {
             "set_hop": {"route": "'turn'"},
             "set_context": {
                 # GH #522 -- TWO keys, because one word was doing two jobs.
                 # `channel_node` is the ADDRESS: the node this turn came out
                 # of, and the word the third edge below routes the answer back
                 # by, because `Edge.to` is static in this substrate and a
                 # container may hold several channels (the address rule, #454).
                 # `channel` is the CHAT: what a surface calls "the same
                 # conversation partner", which is what the session keeper opens
                 # a generation for, what the firewall rate-limits and what a
                 # memory row writes down as the room. Keyed on the node name,
                 # every chat of one connector shared ONE generation, ONE rate
                 # bucket and ONE room -- and the hand-drawn e9-era edge, whose
                 # rows are the history that actually exists, always wrote the
                 # chat id here.
                 "channel_node": "'%s'" % name,
                 "channel": "has(hop.chat_id) ? hop.chat_id : ''",
                 "assistant": "has(context.assistant) && context.assistant != '' "
                              "? context.assistant : (has(hop.addressed_to) && "
                              "hop.addressed_to != '' ? hop.addressed_to : '%s')" % agent,
                 "chat_id": "has(hop.chat_id) ? hop.chat_id : ''",
                 "user_id": "has(hop.user_id) ? hop.user_id : ''",
                 "audience_set": "'[\"agent:%s\",\"member:%s\"]'" % (agent, person)}}},
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.error_code)",
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'error'"}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'answer' && "
                      "has(context.channel_node) && "
                      "context.channel_node == '%s'" % name},
    ]


def _screen_level(place, name, _p):
    # A screen is a channel too -- and it costs two edges, not three: what only
    # a screen produces is `event` and `receipt`, and an agent's ordinary
    # `answer` is the smallest view there is, so the down-edge RESTAMPS it.
    #
    # GH #522 -- both keys, and on a screen they carry the same word. A screen
    # IS one room, so its address and its conversation partner coincide; writing
    # the identity out anyway is what lets every holder downstream go on reading
    # `channel` and every answer go on routing by `channel_node`, whichever kind
    # of channel it came from.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt')",
         "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % name,
                                      "channel": "'%s'" % name}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'answer' || hop.route == 'view') "
                      "&& has(context.channel_node) "
                      "&& context.channel_node == '%s'" % name,
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_view'"}}},
    ]


def _app_level(place, name, p):
    # An app writes onto ONE screen, and what comes back is addressed by the
    # OWNER the display stamped -- the path of the cell that put the view up,
    # never anything the body claims. `hop.owner` is an ABSOLUTE path, so the
    # container stays in the guard whatever the declaration's scope is.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'view' || hop.route == 'error')",
         "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % p["screen"],
                                      "channel": "'%s'" % p["screen"]}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt') "
                      "&& has(hop.owner) && hop.owner.contains('/%s/%s/')"
                      % (place.container, name)},
        # GH #553 -- the mutation receipt. An app draws a picture of something,
        # and the only thing that changes what a picture of a colony shows is a
        # committed mutation; the shipped app (`colony-view`) turns the lane
        # into its own `in_refresh` and the BOOT receipt is what puts the first
        # picture up. It carries no name guard, because an app is addressed by
        # the `hop.owner` the display stamped and a receipt has no owner -- the
        # container and assistant hops of this lane DO carry the permissive name
        # guard (GH #478), and it is the context-less receipt that makes all
        # three of them a fan-out rather than an address.
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'mutation_committed'"},
    ]


# level -> (container it is instantiated into, renderer, extra required params).
# The container is part of the table rather than a parameter: a member does not
# stand in `./people` in one colony and `./members` in another, and a level that
# could be told where it lives would stop being a level. Since GH #503 it is
# also the level's SCOPE, which is the same statement read as an address.
LEVELS = {
    "org":       ("orgs",       _container_level, []),
    "member":    ("members",    _container_level, []),
    "assistant": ("assistants", _assistant_level, []),
    "channel":   ("channels",   _channel_level,   ["assistant"]),
    "screen":    ("channels",   _screen_level,    []),
    "app":       ("apps",       _app_level,       ["screen"]),
}


def grow_level(p):
    level = p["level"]
    container, render, _extra = LEVELS[level]
    # GH #560 -- a generation may be grown with NO key of its own. The switch is
    # opt-in for the same reason the identity door is: writing a person's
    # provider credential into an agent's reach is not something a level does to
    # every generation grown from it without being asked.
    credential = p.get("credential") if level == "assistant" else None
    # The narrow form for every level, and the two exceptions are reachability
    # facts rather than a taste. An identity door reaches the container's
    # SIBLING `./affinity`, which no declaration standing in the container can
    # name -- written out at the branch that draws it, in `_assistant_level`.
    # The credential road reaches the member's own `./access`, one storey up in
    # the same way. An edge lives in the graph of the lowest common ancestor of
    # its endpoints, so either switch moves the whole declaration to the member.
    place = Place(container, not (level == "assistant"
                                  and (p.get("subscribe") or credential)))
    node = {"name": place.node(p["name"]), "template": p["template"]}
    if isinstance(p.get("override_params"), dict):
        node["override_params"] = p["override_params"]
    if credential:
        node["override_params"] = _credential_overrides(
            node.get("override_params"), p["name"], credential)
    # The birth state travels TOP-LEVEL on the entry, beside `template` and not
    # inside `override_params`: it is a property of the placement and not of a
    # cell's own settings, it covers the whole subtree the node brings, and the
    # door reads it exactly there (GH #472).
    birth = p.get("birth") or LEVEL_BIRTH.get(level)
    if birth:
        node["birth"] = birth
    # ONE declaration, and since GH #567 that holds for the credential road too:
    # the node, its edges and the grants that answer them are one decision, and
    # a manifest rolls forward with no rollback -- a node that landed without
    # its edges is an island, which is the failure this recipe exists to
    # prevent. The credential edges come LAST, behind the level's own, and the
    # grants ride in the same diff.
    ctx = p.get("ctx") if isinstance(p.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
    diff = {"add_nodes": [node], "add_edges": render(place, p["name"], p)}
    if credential:
        now = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
               .strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"))
        diff["add_edges"] = (diff["add_edges"]
                             + _credential_edges(p["name"], credential))
        diff["seed_rows"] = _credential_rows(p["name"], credential, now)
    return [{"scope": place.scope(p["scope"]), "ctx": ctx, "diff": diff}]


RENDER = {"rewire_edge": rewire_edge, "add_node": add_node,
          "attach_drain": attach_drain, "grow_level": grow_level}


# --- the screen a member always gets (GH #543, ruling R-0904-4) -------------
#
# A person in this substrate is the thing that HAS input and output devices.
# Whether they use them is a second question; that they have them is not one at
# all -- so a member wish grows the person AND the screen it speaks through and
# the application that draws on it. There is no `screen: false`: `classify`
# drops a falsy key, so a tri-state would be indistinguishable from a wish that
# never mentioned it, and the ruling has no third state to distinguish anyway.
#
# The NAMES are fixed here for the same reason the container of a level is
# (`LEVELS`): a member does not stand in `./people` in one colony and
# `./members` in another, and a screen that can be renamed is a wish choosing
# again. What is NOT fixed here is which TEMPLATE fills them, or where the port
# band starts -- those are the builder's own configuration (`doc["params"]`),
# because the builder is part of the OS and the OS is what hands out what is
# system-near (ADR-0022).
MEMBER_SCREEN = "display"
MEMBER_APP = "colony-view"


class PortUnallocatable(Exception):
    """The port could not be worked out, so no port is handed out.

    It wears `count_unavailable`, the same code `templates/builder/tally` speaks
    when the count itself could not be taken -- because it is the same event seen
    one cell later: the OS was asked for a port and cannot answer. The repair is
    the same too (look at the builder's own configuration, or at why the count
    came back unreadable), which is the test for whether two facts deserve one
    code.

    It is NOT a fall-back to index 0. A screen quietly given the base port is a
    second holder of a socket somebody else already has, and the failure surfaces
    as a page that never loads -- the silent class this whole allocation exists
    to prevent. An ABSENT index still means zero: nobody counted, so this is the
    first member, and that is a statement rather than a guess.
    """


def _whole(value, what):
    """`value` as an int, or a named refusal. Empty and absent mean zero."""
    text = str(value if value is not None else "").strip()
    if text == "":
        return 0
    try:
        return int(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise PortUnallocatable(
            "%s is %r, which is not a number, so the port of this member's "
            "screen cannot be worked out. No port is handed out rather than a "
            "wrong one: two screens on one socket is one screen and one silent "
            "degradation." % (what, text))

# The defaults, used when the instance overrides nothing.
DEFAULT_SETTINGS = {"member_screen_template": "display@1.0.2",
                    "member_app_template": "colony-view@1.1.0",
                    "screen_port_base": 7900}


def member_devices(p, settings, index):
    """The devices half of a member wish: its screen, and the app on it.

    TWO declarations and not one, because a screen stands in `channels` and an
    app in `apps`: two containers are two scope roots since GH #503, and a
    declaration has exactly one. They travel BEHIND the person in the same
    manifest because they are one decision -- a screen nobody draws on and an
    app with nothing to draw on are each half an act, and a person without
    either is the silent failure GH #585 measured.

    The PORT is `screen_port_base + index`, written as `override_params` on the
    screen's own node. It is not in the wish and not in the template: a port is
    system-near, one socket is one screen, and the index is MEASURED off
    `/colony/graph` by the cell in front of this one rather than claimed by the
    caller (GH #517 is what a claimed coordinate costs).
    """
    # The member's own PATH, which is not the scope the wish named: a member
    # wish says "under /os/orgs/acme" and the person stands one storey below
    # that, in the container the level declares itself at (GH #503). Read off
    # `Place` rather than spelled again, so the two cannot disagree.
    container, _render, _extra = LEVELS["member"]
    member = "%s/%s" % (Place(container, True).scope(p["scope"]), p["name"])
    port = (_whole(settings["screen_port_base"], "the builder's screen_port_base")
            + _whole(index, "hop.member_index"))
    screen = grow_level({"scope": member, "level": "screen",
                         "name": MEMBER_SCREEN,
                         "template": settings["member_screen_template"],
                         "override_params": {"web": {"port": port}}})
    app = grow_level({"scope": member, "level": "app", "name": MEMBER_APP,
                      "template": settings["member_app_template"],
                      "screen": MEMBER_SCREEN})
    return screen + app


def read_settings(params):
    """The three values an instance may set, defaulted where it set none."""
    out = dict(DEFAULT_SETTINGS)
    for key in DEFAULT_SETTINGS:
        value = (params or {}).get(key)
        if value not in (None, ""):
            out[key] = value
    return out

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)


def hop_of(document):
    """The routing keys the message arrived with. `code` cells read them off the
    envelope; the only one this recipe wants is `member_index`."""
    return ((document.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {}


msgs = doc["body"].get("messages") or []
payload = {}
for m in msgs:
    if m.get("text"):
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m["text"])
        except Exception:
            payload = {}

recipe = payload.get("recipe")
if recipe not in RENDER:
    # Cannot happen after `classify` -- and it is here anyway, because a cell
    # knows no topology and must not build on who stands in front of it.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "recipe_unknown"},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "no renderer for %r" % recipe})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

params = payload.get("params") or {}
if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("level") not in LEVELS:
    # Named, never guessed at. A level the table does not carry is a level whose
    # edge set nobody has written down, and rendering "something close" would
    # produce a subtree that boots and answers nothing.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "level_unknown",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "no level by that name",
                                          "level": str(params.get("level")),
                                          "known": sorted(LEVELS)})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)
if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("birth") \
        and params.get("birth") not in BIRTH_STATES:
    # Named, never guessed at -- the same rule the level name follows. The door
    # refuses an unknown birth state pre-destructively, so nothing would be lost
    # by passing it through; what would be lost is the NAME of the refusal, one
    # hop away from the wish that made it.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "birth_unknown",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "no birth state by that name",
                                          "birth": str(params.get("birth")),
                                          "known": sorted(BIRTH_STATES)})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)
try:
    decls = RENDER[recipe](params)
except WishIncomplete as w:
    # GH #517 -- the wish did not say, so the recipe ASKS. It wears the code the
    # design lane already uses for exactly this act (`normalise`, a composer
    # that answers with a question instead of inventing a model id), because
    # the two are the same event on two lanes: a build that stopped because it
    # was not told enough, with the missing thing named in words a human can
    # answer.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "wish_incomplete",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": w.question,
                                          "missing": ["ctx.%s" % w.key]})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)
except KeyError as e:
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "recipe_params_incomplete",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "missing parameter %s" % e})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

# GH #543 -- a member wish renders the person AND the screen and the app that
# person always gets, in that order: the devices draw into `<member>/channels`
# and `<member>/apps`, scopes only the person creates.
#
# GH #585 -- and they leave as ONE SUBMISSION. The order between them is
# semantics, and a front has no ordering across two submissions handed over in
# the same turn: measured on a fresh colony, the devices reached the door first
# and were refused with `edge_schema` for a scope that did not exist yet, while
# the person committed behind them -- a member without a screen and without an
# app, and a wish that reported success. Inside ONE manifest the order is the
# door's to keep: the colony rolls a manifest off entry by entry through the
# very `handle_mutation` a single body takes, so an entry is judged against the
# tree the entries in front of it just grew (measured in
# `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh585_a_member_wish_is_one_submission.rs`). The
# roll-forward still has no rollback, so the order is not a preference; it is
# now inside the one document that carries it.
#
# `doc["params"]` is read HERE and nowhere else, and it is the only thing this
# cell reads beyond its own stdin: no network, no disk, no retrieval. What it
# says is which template fills the two devices and where the port band starts --
# the instance's own configuration, set with `override_params` on the builder.
manifests = [decls]
if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("level") == "member":
    settings = read_settings(doc.get("params"))
    # The index the counting cell in front of this one measured off
    # `/colony/graph`. ABSENT means "nobody counted", and the base port is what a
    # first member gets -- a bind collision is a survivable, message-repairable
    # event (`WebEvent::BindFailed`), never a boot failure. Present and
    # UNREADABLE is a different fact and gets a different answer, one cell down
    # in `member_devices`: it is named, never rounded down to zero.
    try:
        manifests = [decls + member_devices(
            params, settings, hop_of(doc).get("member_index"))]
    except PortUnallocatable as e:
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
            "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "count_unavailable",
                       "recipe": recipe},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                          "text": json.dumps({"reason": str(e)})}]}))
        sys.exit(0)

out = []
for one in manifests:
    sha = digest(one)
    out.append({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "manifest_class": "fast",
                   "manifest_sha256": sha, "declaration_count": len(one)},
        "manifest": one,
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "%s: %d declaration(s), scope %s" % (
                          recipe, len(one), one[0].get("scope", "?"))}]})

# GH #480 -- the fast lane writes down what a refusal will need, and it is the
# same two rows the design lane already writes.
#
# A refused submission comes back on `in_receipt`, which arrives on a FOREIGN
# chain by construction: `templates/submit/gate` renders the receipt off its own
# remembered row, so nothing of this build's context survives the round trip.
# `weave` recovers a composed build from two rows -- `normalise`'s digest
# binding, which says who owns those bytes, and the caller row, which says which
# door the answer goes to. A recipe wrote neither, so a refused fast-lane build
# ended as `build_unknown` and was delivered into `./orgs` rather than to the
# operator that asked (measured: `template_missing`, GH #480).
#
# The build id IS the digest. A fast-lane build has no other identity -- no
# composer opened a round to mint one -- and the digest is the one handle that
# survives the submitter's chain, because the submitter parks and pops a
# submission under it.
#
# `build_lane` is the third thing the row says, and it is the reason the row can
# be read at all: a model-free build has no composer, no thread and no question,
# so its refusal must NOT enter the repair machine. `weave` reads the marker off
# this row and takes the short road instead -- name the code, answer the door.
#
# Nothing is written for a REFUSED recipe: a build that produced no bytes has no
# digest to be refused under, and a row nobody can reach is a slate that only
# grows. And nothing is written when the context names NO caller at all -- the
# same guard `weave` parks its own row under (`names_a_caller`). There is no door
# to recover then, because none was ever stamped, and a slate written for a build
# nobody is waiting on is a table that only grows.
ctx = ((doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
caller = {k: str(ctx.get(k) or "") for k in CALLER_KEYS}
names_a_caller = any(caller.values())
caller["build_lane"] = "recipe"
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def parked(build_id, slot, role, turn):
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": slot,
            "text": json.dumps({
                "operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
                "row": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": 0, "role": role,
                        "turn": turn, "fired": 0, "recorded_at": now}})}


# `operation` is `bind` and not `recipe`: BOTH `./recipes -> .` edges match on
# `hop.operation == 'recipe'`, so a binding wearing that operation would leave
# the hive as a second answer to the same wish.
#
# ONE PAIR PER MANIFEST. `weave` finds the caller row by `build_id == <digest>`,
# and a manifest is refused or committed under its own digest, so a build that
# wrote no pair for a manifest it emitted would leave that manifest's refusal
# with no door to answer to -- the exact `build_unknown` failure GH #480
# measured for the fast lane as a whole. Since GH #585 a member wish emits one
# manifest, so it writes one pair; the loop stays because the rule is per
# manifest and not per wish.
if names_a_caller:
    for one in manifests:
        one_sha = digest(one)
        out.append({
            "header": {"route": "bind", "operation": "bind",
                       "manifest_sha256": one_sha},
            "messages": [parked(one_sha, "w-fast-caller", "caller",
                                json.dumps(caller)),
                         parked(one_sha, "w-fast-bind", "manifest", one_sha)]})
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))

member_screen_template.description: The template the screen every member gets is instantiated from (GH #543). It lives on the BUILDER and not in the wish: a member does not choose whether it has a screen, and the recipe does not choose what fills one -- a template is a catalogue question. Colony-wide, which in a colony carrying one organisation is the same statement as `the org assigns it`; a real per-org surface does not exist in the substrate (org is a namespace, `HiveParams` is deny_unknown_fields, and no read endpoint hands params out).

member_app_template.description: The template the application that draws on that screen is instantiated from (GH #543). Same argument, same place: a screen nobody draws on is half an act, so the two are configured together and rendered together.

screen_port_base.description: The first port of the band a member's screen takes (GH #543). The screen gets `screen_port_base + <the member's index in the organisation>`, and the index is MEASURED off /colony/graph by `tally` in front of this cell, never claimed by the wish. A port is system-near and the OS is what allocates it (ADR-0022); the builder is part of the OS. A taken port is a survivable event -- the `web` cell answers `BindFailed`, keeps its task and binds on the next address it is given -- so a base that collides is a diagnosis rather than a boot failure.

member_index.description: How many members the organisation already carries, measured off /colony/graph by `tally` and stamped on the wish before it gets here (GH #543). Read for a member wish and ignored for every other level; absent means nobody counted, and the first member's port is the base itself.

description.purpose: The fast lane: four predefined recipes rendered straight from their parameters into a manifest, with its sha256 digest. No model, no network, no disk -- what leaves here is a string built out of a dict. The fourth is grow_level, which renders the transit edge set a composition level gives a new child: it is the same set every time, so it is a table here rather than a paragraph a model rewrites per build. The counts live in the README, once, and a test derives them from this renderer. Two things ride BESIDE that set: a `birth` state written top-level on the node -- the door's own vocabulary, and a channel is rendered `inactive` because a connector opens its upstream the moment it has a task -- and, for an assistant and only when the wish asks, the identity door: the push edge from the member's own affinity record plus the receipt drain beside it. Since GH #543 a MEMBER wish renders the person AND the screen and the application that person always gets, on a port this cell adds to its own base; since GH #585 the three ride in ONE manifest, in dependency order, because two submissions handed to a front in the same turn have no order at all and the devices draw into scopes only the person creates.
description.use_when: Behind `classify` on hop.route == 'recipe', when the caller named a recipe and its parameters are complete.
description.not_in_scope: No inference, no retrieval, no application. No template CHOICE either: grow_level renders edges and is TOLD which template to instantiate -- by the wish, or, for the screen a member always gets, by its own configuration -- because what a level should be filled with is a catalogue question and the catalogue is the librarian's. And no RETRIEVAL for the port either: the member's index in its organisation is measured by the cell in front of this one and arrives as a hop key, so this cell still reads nothing but its stdin. And no number GUESSED: an index or a port base that arrived unreadable is refused as `count_unavailable`, because a screen quietly given the base port is a second holder of somebody else's socket. No subscription ROW either: writing one is a store write and not a mutation declaration, so it stays a `subscribe` op through affinity's own gate -- what is rendered here is the graph that row will need. And no rollback to lean on: the order of the declarations is semantics, because a manifest rolls forward and stops at the first refusal. And no ROUND to invent: the audience a grown channel's turns are spoken in is read off the wish's own `ctx` (`member_person`) and a wish that does not name it is asked, because a round is provenance and a wrong one blanks the whole memory behind a gate that is working exactly as specified (GH #517).
